title: Zeros of Pick and Hopf Differentials and Fences of Convex Domains
summary: arXiv:2611.24022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the vanishing order of a Pick or Hopf differential controls the corresponding convex domain through sharp disk comparisons. For a complete hyperbolic affine sphere, Pick vanishing order $m\ge0$ gives normalized projective coordinates in which the domain lies between disks of radii $\sqrt{\cos(\pi/(m+3))}$ and its reciprocal. For a harmonic diffeomorphism to a convex hyperbolic domain with complete $\partial$-energy metric, Hopf vanishing order $m$ gives a disk in the image of radius $\log\cot(\pi/(2(m+2)))$, centered at the image point. Equality characterizes the corresponding regular polygons. For polygonal targets, these comparisons prove the Fence conjecture of Dumas--Wolf and give explicit Hilbert and hyperbolic distance bounds for higher fences. We also construct simple-zero examples showing that these sufficient multiplicity conditions are not necessary.

title: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups
summary: arXiv:2611.23852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.

title: Worst-case bias of the independence assumption for functions of two ordinal variables
summary: arXiv:2611.24439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let ordinal grades $X$ and $Y$ be obtained by cutting a pair of random variables with copula $C$ at arbitrary thresholds, and let $g$ be a function of the grades. We study the largest error $S_C(g)$, over all thresholds, that is, over all marginal laws, made when the mean of $g(X,Y)$ is computed as if the grades were independent. This is the counterpart of the classical dependence-uncertainty problem: the copula is fixed and the discretisation is free. The error is caused entirely by the interaction of the inputs, measured by an index $\rho(g)$, the largest absolute $g$-volume of a rectangle of grades, which vanishes if and only if $g$ is additive. For every copula, $S_C(g)$ lies between $\rho(g)$ times the largest deviation of $C$ from the independence copula and $\rho(g)$ times half the total variation of their difference, and the factor one half cannot be improved. For the Gaussian copula with correlation $\lambda$ we prove that $S_C(g)$ equals $|\lambda|\rho(g)/(2\pi)$ to first order, with a sharp constant and an explicit remainder.
